L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is stavudine (d4T), a thymine 2',3'-didehydro-2',3'-dideoxynucleoside. Closely related pyrimidine dideoxynucleosides have measured absolute oral bioavailability well above 20%: emtricitabine 92% fasted and 93% in multiple reports, lamivudine 68.6–93% across formulations, and zalcitabine 80% (54–127%) in humans; even the less bioavailable nucleoside cladribine is 36–46%.

L4 intestinal absorption records show that AZT, which shares the thymine base, has a human fraction absorbed of 98% and >90% gastrointestinal absorption at 60 mg/kg in an animal study; thymine solubility in FeSSIF is 6.2 ± 0.2 mg/mL, supporting adequate dissolution for this low-logD nucleoside scaffold.
L3 lamivudine oral exposure records show rapid absorption (median Tmax 0.75–1.26 h) and measurable Cmax after oral dosing, consistent with high oral bioavailability in this nucleoside class.

L5 gut-wall/intestinal records classify AZT as high permeability (P_eff 4.17 ± 0.43 × 10^-5 cm/s) and lamivudine as moderate-to-high permeability (P_eff 3.08 ± 0.26 × 10^-5 cm/s); no supplied record provides affirmative gut-wall efflux or intestinal-metabolism evidence for F < 20% for stavudine.

Didanosine's low/variable F (0.22–0.28, 29 ± 6%, <40%, range 2–89%) is formulation- and acid-lability-dependent and is not transferable to stavudine; the single mouse zalcitabine value of 30% is species-limited and outweighed by the human value of 80%.

L6 hepatic-clearance records concern AZT (3'-azido-3'-deoxythymidine) and 5-ethyl-AzddU, not stavudine. AZT has substantial UGT-mediated hepatic clearance (in vivo 19 ml/min/kg; hepatocyte-scaled 15.1 ml/min/kg) and 5-ethyl-AzddU is a UDPGT substrate, but stavudine lacks the 3'-azido group and no stavudine-specific hepatic-clearance or metabolic-stability measurement is supplied; these records do not provide affirmative evidence for F < 20% for stavudine.

evidence_gaps: No direct stavudine absolute-bioavailability record is present; prediction relies on structural transfer from closely related pyrimidine dideoxynucleosides and AZT.
No query-specific IV comparison, AUC, Cmax, dose, or formulation data are supplied.
No stavudine-specific hepatic clearance or metabolic-stability measurement is available; L6 AZT/5-ethyl-AzddU records are not directly transferable.
Food effects and first-pass metabolic/clearance contributions for stavudine are not directly measured in the cited records.
Didanosine's low/variable F is formulation- and acid-sensitivity-dependent and is not treated as transferable negative evidence.
